actions.note: At 2 and 4 s the faucet stream visibly contacts cupped/rubbing hands before the later soap-bar and lather views.
At 6 s a greenish soap bar is held and rubbed between the hands beside and under the flowing faucet. The visible bar contact supports soap application.

At 12 s the hands rub together away from the water stream and a thin whitish soapy patch is visible on the hand/finger surfaces. This supports rubbing with lather rather than just standing at the sink.
At 16, 20, and 24 s, after the cited lather-rubbing view, the hands are placed directly under the visible water stream and rotated through it.

The follow-up views at 24.5, 25, and 25.5 s show hands still under or beside the running water, then the hand moves out of view at 26 s. From 26.5 through 31.936 s the images show the faucet stream and empty basin. No towel-paper wiping or visibly operating hand dryer contacts the hands in these supplied images.
